messages:
kat: ok, prototyping a new synthetic traffic generator for apples-to-apples kernel/batching perf runs. goal: deterministic burst patterns + long-tail shaping so we can reproduce perf regressions.

mike: nice — what's different from the other harnesses?

kat: two diffs: 1) phase-aligned QPS ramps so we can create constructive/destructive wave interference across replicas, 2) a KV 'splay' model to simulate cold->warm key accesses plus explicit warmup windows. plus deterministic seed for replay.

anya: can you paste an example config? i want to run this against 8xA100 and a 4xH100 comparison matrix.

kat: sure, quick config snippet:

```
mode: "phase_ramp"
seed: 482913
phases: [ {qps:1000, dur:60}, {qps:3000, dur:30}, {qps:600, dur:120} ]
kv_model: { skew: "zipf", warm_pct: 0.68, ttl_ms: 120000 }
batching: { strategy: "adaptive_queue_length", max_latency_ms: 25 }
replay: { deterministic: true, snapshot: "splineburst-482913.snap" }
```

kevin: how do you model KV cache eviction & warmup in that config? we need realistic eviction churn to stress kv cache behavior.

kat: kv_model.ttl_ms + warm_pct control occupancy. the harness supports a prefill window: we can run a warmup phase that emits only hot keys at high QPS for N seconds to load the cache, then switch to the mixed pattern. eviction churn comes from a configurable background churn rate to simulate competing tenants.

mike: and batching heuristics? we need to compare fixed small batches vs our adaptive queue-length heuristic.

kat: generator supports modes: fixed_qps, adaptive_queue_length, bursty_buckets. it emits metrics for wait_in_queue, actual_batch_size, batch_size_hist and kernel_choice per step so we can correlate kernel selection with batch size distribution.

anya: i ran a quick profile yesterday — on fp16 kernels kernel fallback spiked when avg_batch_size < 8, we saw runtime choose aten_mm frequently which is faster per-request for tiny batches but loses when latency tail grows.

kat: fyi, replay at ~3k qps mid-tail showed kernel-selection thrash: runtime flipped between aten_mm and fused_attention based on micro-fluctuations in queue depth. that flip-flop caused context-switch overhead and ~12% p95 regression vs a steady-state run.

kevin: can you paste a short log excerpt from the thrashed run?

kat: sure:

```
[00:12:03.432] kernel_select: batch_size=6 -> choose aten_mm
[00:12:03.439] kernel_select: batch_size=11 -> choose fused_attention
[00:12:03.447] kernel_select: batch_size=5 -> choose aten_mm
[00:12:03.455] kernel_select: batch_size=12 -> choose fused_attention
... (repeats)
```

mike: reproduce steps? i can run the replay on canary.

kat: replay harness CLI: 

```
./splineburst run --config splineburst-482913.yaml --seed 482913 --target hosts=@canary --duration 10m --collect perf_counters,kernel_trace
```

anya: i prototyped a simple fix: hysteresis on kernel selection using a 2s exponential moving average of batch_size before switching kernels. in staging that cut the p95 regression by ~9% (not perfect but much lower thrash).

kevin: also consider kv-affinity: prefer kernels that support efficient KV cache reuse when kv_occupancy > 0.7, even if batch size is marginally lower. that keeps memory layouts stable.

kat: good call. plan: add hysteresis + kv_affinity flag to generator and add a 3x apples-to-apples sweep: (A) fixed batching, (B) adaptive queuing, (C) adaptive + hysteresis + kv_affinity. pin model version, seq_len, and host topology for each run. measure p50/p95/p99 + tokens/s + kernel_switch_rate.

mike: please also output the replay seed and the full env (NUMA, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, driver) in the run-artifact so ops can reproduce binary-identical runs.

ci-bot: perf-run queued: splineburst/nightly/2815 (will notify when complete) :rocket:

anya: i'll open PR with hysteresis patch and attach a small harness README with sample commands + seed. tagging @kat for review.

kat: thanks — if everyone uses the same seed and pinned infra we should get deterministic apples-to-apples comparisons and be able to bisect kernel perf regressions reliably. i'll add a short section about long-tail shaping and how to interpret the burst phase interference graphs. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

mike: sweet. once PR is in let's schedule a 30m run vs the current canary and post the metrics to the perf dashboard.

kevin: one more note: include a toggle to inject random tiny background noise (gaussian jitter) to avoid overfitting to perfectly periodic patterns. some regressions only appear with small stochasticity.

kat: added to backlog. thanks all.
